'''Antonio Eusebio Lazcano Araujo Reyes''' (born 1950) is a Mexican [[biology]] [[researcher]] and [[professor]] of the  School of Sciences at the [[Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México|National Autonomous University of Mexico]]  in [[Mexico City]].<ref>[http://www.fciencias.unam.mx/biologia/evolutiva/Personal.html List of Staff in the Faculty of Science, UNAM] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161101015358/http://www.fciencias.unam.mx/biologia/evolutiva/Personal.html |date=2016-11-01 }} Retrieved December 2010</ref><ref name="resume">[http://www.iquimica.unam.mx/simposio/cv_ALAR.html Resume of Antonio Lazcano at UNAM] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090615005512/http://www.iquimica.unam.mx/simposio/cv_ALAR.html |date=June 15, 2009 }} (Last updated c. 2002) Retrieved December 2010</ref> He has studied the origin and early [[evolution]] of life for more than 35 years.{{Citation needed|date=December 2010}}

Lazcano pursued his undergraduate and graduate studies focused on the study of [[prebiotic evolution]] and the [[abiogenesis|emergence of life]]. He has been professor-in-residence or visiting scientist in France, Spain, Cuba, Switzerland, Russia, and the United States.<ref name="resume" /> He has written several books in Spanish, including ''The Origin of Life'' (1984) which became a best-seller with more than 600,000 sold copies.{{Citation needed|date=December 2010}}In addition, he has been a member of several advisoryand review boards of scientific organizations, such as [[NASA]], where he was a member of the [[NASA Astrobiology Institute]]<ref>[https://nai.nasa.gov/directory/lazcano-antonio/ NASA Astrobiology profile Antonio Lazcano] Retrieved December 2010</ref>

He served as president of the [[ISSOL|International Society for the Study of the Origin of Life]], for two terms,<ref>[http://issol.org/meetings/ Past ICOL/ISSOL Meetings] Retrieved December 2010</ref> and is also the first Latin American scientist to occupy this position.  A great honor, for [[Alexander Oparin]], [[Stanley L. Miller]] and [[J. William Schopf]], were also presidents of ISSOL.

Lazcano has devoted considerable efforts to promote [[scientific journalism]] and teaching. He also promotes the study of [[evolutionary biology]] and the origins of life, all over the world.
